column1: # profiles.tsv — the process profiles: what a kind of change owes, as data. Four scripts read it:
# scripts/pr-triage.sh (types, paths, tier, standing), scripts/trailers-lint.sh (types, trailers),
# scripts/land.sh (types, freeze) and scripts/ready.sh (the declarable rows: types `-`).
# Format: seven TAB-separated columns per row; blank lines and lines starting with # are
# ignored (the conventions of doc-owners.tsv).
#   name      a lowercase word, unique
#   types     the title types the row applies to, comma-separated: `*` any, `breaking` a title with
#             `!` or a `BREAKING CHANGE` line; `-` none: the row applies only when `make ready
#             PROFILE=<name>` declares it (the message then carries `Profile: <name>`)
#   paths     an ERE over the production paths of the change; `-` any (also a change with none)
#   tier      the review tier floor: `full`, or `-`
#   trailers  the lines `make ready` requires in the message, comma-separated (`Found-by`,
#             `Introduced-by`: scripts/trailers-lint.sh checks their values), or `-`;
#             only a row whose paths are `-` can require any: ready knows the message
#   freeze    `held`: the lander holds a change of these types while the release freeze is open
#   standing  `no`: a standing approval may not queue it, or `-`
# EVERY row whose types and paths both match applies, and for each column the strictest value
# wins: the highest tier floor, the union of the trailers, `held` over `-`, `no` over `-`. There
# is no first match: a `fix(mcp):` in an invariant area is `fix` and `security` at once, so it is
# full tier and still owes its trailers. Fail closed, per reader: a missing file, a row
# with another number of fields, or an unknown value in a column the script reads, makes
# pr-triage.sh (tier, freeze, standing, a path pattern that is no ERE), trailers-lint.sh (an
# unknown trailer name) and land.sh (the freeze column) exit 2, naming the row. ready.sh reads
# the name and types columns only and refuses an undeclared PROFILE.
# security: packages whose invariants are written down outside the code (an area AGENTS.md) or
# are about security and concurrency. process: what runs on, or gets installed into, users'
# machines without being Go code, and the files agents execute (D857, D955): at any size a full
# review, never a standing merge.
